newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon calls May 17 legislative election.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon calls May 17 legislative election.

text.p: Cameroon will hold a parliamentary election on May 17, President Paul Biya announced in a decree on Wednesday.
The election will be the second legislative poll since the Central African nation began its sometimes turbulent transition to multi-party democracy in 1990.
The announcement coincides with tension in Cameroon's volatile English-speaking North-west province, where clashes between attackers and security forces have killed 10 people.

Communication Minister Augustin Kontchou Koumegni said on Monday that the government would take appropriate steps to ensure polling would go ahead in the province. An overnight curfew is already in force.

Kontchou declined to speculate on the identity of the attackers but police blame English-speaking separatists trying to steal arms and ammunition from security forces in the provincial capital Bamenda and nearby towns.
The opposition Social Democratic Front of John Fru Ndi had accused the government of dirty tricks and seeking an excuse to postpone the poll in the province.
Kontchou said that three paramilitary gendarmes and seven attackers had been killed in the attacks.
Part of the opposition boycotted the last parliamentary poll in 1992. Biya supporters secured a majority after allying with a minor party. The May poll was initially planned for March.
Biya, who took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982, faces a presidential election in October.
